page.overview:
What is Iron Crown?

The Iron Crown of Morgoth, also called the Iron Crown or Morgoth's crown, was the great crown forged by Morgoth after his return to Middle-earth, to emphasize his claim to the mantle of King of the World

In the year 1495 of the Years of the Trees, as a vast "iron-crownéd" helm. With each fastened the three Silmarils were set into the crown. Morgoth treasured the Silmarils in his crown above anything else. In the year 456, after the Dagor Bragollach in the year 455, Morgoth was "iron-crowned" when he came out of Angband's gates to meet Fingolfin's challenge.

By the year 465, the Silmarils had become famous "throughout the world" as a consequence of tales spread by Mólanoldorin Elves "had seen them...blazing lustrous in the" Iron Crown of Morgoth. that he could only be with Lúthien if he fetched him a Silmaril as a "bride-price" Only then, could he be with Lúthien if she still desired. During the Quest of the Silmaril early in the year 466, Lúthien, after sneaking into Angband with Beren, cast a spell of sleep upon Morgoth, and as he fell to the ground, the Iron Crown rolled away. After Lúthien roused Beren, they attempted to move the crown, but failed. As a consequence of laboring noiselessly, and the blade-shard smote Morgoth's cheek, causing him to groan When Beren and Lúthien returned to Doriath, Thingol reminded Beren that he said he wouldn't return without a Silmaril "from the crown of Morgoth". In the year 587, after Morgoth's defeat by the Host of Valinor in the War of Wrath, the other two jewels were removed, and the crown was beaten by the Valar "into a collar for his neck".

On Thursday, October 6 in the year 3018 of the late Third Age, after singing an excerpt from the long Lay of Lúthien on Weathertop in the Weather Hills to distract Frodo Baggins, Meriadoc Brandybuck, Peregrin Took, and Samwise Gamgee from their fears, Aragorn II summarized the lay and explained its history and form to the Hobbits, mentioning the "iron crown" Beren and Lúthien took the Great Jewel from. March 11 in the year 3019, after "walking and climbing for" probably "well over twenty-four hours", Sam and Frodo took a rest "in a dark crevice" and ate "their last meal" before entering Mordor in the Ephel Dúath above Imlad Morgul. As they talked about tales and adventures, Sam mentioned the "Iron Crown in Thangorodrim" to Frodo while mentioning Beren's renowned quest.
